## 1) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug
Consensus: 3/3 reviewers
Title: Implement abstract methods on `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` or keep it a concrete stub

Affected:
- src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py:11-12

Explanation:
`MetricAlertDetectorHandler` now subclasses `StatefulDetectorHandler`, but its body is only `pass`. `StatefulDetectorHandler` is an `abc.ABC` that declares these abstract methods:
- `get_dedupe_value`
- `get_group_key_values`
- `build_occurrence_and_event_data`, which this diff adds as a new `@abc.abstractmethod`

The class also does not define `counter_names`.

Because none of these are implemented, the class can no longer be instantiated. When `Detector.detector_handler` instantiates the handler for a metric-alert detector, Python raises `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class`.

`process_detectors` has no exception handling around `detector.detector_handler`. A single metric-alert detector in the list therefore aborts evaluation for every detector in the batch.

Before this change, the handler was a safe no-op that returned `[]`. No test exercises the metric-alert group type, so the test suite does not catch this.

To fix it, do one of the following:
- Keep the class as a concrete `DetectorHandler` stub that returns `{}` until the stateful implementation is ready.
- Implement all the abstract methods.

Proposed fix:
~~~python
# Option A: concrete no-op stub until implemented
class MetricAlertDetectorHandler(DetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]):
    def evaluate(
        self, data_packet: DataPacket[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]
    ) -> dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]:
        # TODO: Implement as StatefulDetectorHandler
        return {}

# Option B: implement the abstract hooks
class MetricAlertDetectorHandler(StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]):
    def get_dedupe_value(self, data_packet: DataPacket[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]) -> int:
        return 0

    def get_group_key_values(
        self, data_packet: DataPacket[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]
    ) -> dict[DetectorGroupKey, int]:
        return {}

    def build_occurrence_and_event_data(
        self, group_key: DetectorGroupKey, value: int, new_status: PriorityLevel
    ) -> tuple[IssueOccurrence, dict[str, Any]]:
        raise NotImplementedError
~~~

## 2) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Consensus: 1/3 reviewers
Title: Build the occurrence before enqueuing the state update

Affected:
- src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py:286-301

Explanation:
`enqueue_state_update(group_key, is_active, new_status)` runs before `build_occurrence_and_event_data` is called. Two things after that point can raise:
- The new hook is subclass-provided code and may throw.
- `PriorityLevel(new_status)` can raise `ValueError` if a `DetectorPriorityLevel` value has no matching `PriorityLevel` member.

If either raises, the handler already holds a pending state update marking the group as active. If that update is later committed, the stored state says the group is active, but no occurrence was ever produced. Later evaluations then see no status change, so the issue is never created.

The fix is to compute the result first and enqueue the state update only afterwards.

Proposed fix:
~~~python
is_active = new_status != DetectorPriorityLevel.OK
event_data = None
result: StatusChangeMessage | IssueOccurrence
if new_status == DetectorPriorityLevel.OK:
    result = StatusChangeMessage(...)
else:
    result, event_data = self.build_occurrence_and_event_data(
        group_key, value, PriorityLevel(new_status)
    )
self.enqueue_state_update(group_key, is_active, new_status)
~~~

## 3) Severity: LOW | Type: Test
Consensus: 1/3 reviewers
Title: Use the actual evaluated values when building expected occurrences

Affected:
- tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py:190-192
- tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py:489-491
- tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py:509-511

Explanation:
Expected occurrences are built with `value=6`, but the values actually evaluated differ:
- `test_state_results_multi_group` evaluates `group_2` with 10.
- `test_results_on_change` evaluates with 100.
- `test_dedupe` evaluates with 8.

These tests pass only because the mock builder ignores `value`. As a result:
- A regression that passes the wrong value to `build_occurrence_and_event_data` would go unnoticed.
- Readers are misled about what is being asserted.

Pass the real values, and include `value` in the mock occurrence so that mismatches fail.

Proposed fix:
~~~python
occurrence_2, event_data_2 = build_mock_occurrence_and_event(
    detector.detector_handler, "group_2", 10, PriorityLevel.HIGH
)
# and in build_mock_occurrence_and_event:
evidence_data={"value": value},
~~~

## 4) Severity: LOW | Type: Doc
Consensus: 1/3 reviewers
Title: Update the `evaluate` docstring to describe the dict return type

Affected:
- src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py:226-231

Explanation:
`evaluate` now returns a dict keyed by group key. The docstring still says it "returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`". This is misleading to callers, who might iterate over the keys instead of the values.

Proposed fix:
~~~python
"""
Evaluates a given data packet and returns a dict of `DetectorEvaluationResult` keyed by group key.
"""
~~~

## 5) Severity: LOW | Type: Performance
Consensus: 1/3 reviewers
Title: Make serial per-result Kafka produces on the hot path visible

Affected:
- src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py:60-62

Explanation:
Previously, non-OK transitions produced `result=None`. Now every transition into an active state builds an `IssueOccurrence` and calls `produce_occurrence_to_kafka`. These calls happen serially inside the per-detector, per-group-key loop.

When a packet fans out to many group keys, the cost depends on producer behaviour:
- It is cheap if produce is fire-and-forget.
- It is expensive if produce blocks or flushes per message.

Suggested mitigations:
- Verify that the producer does not block per call.
- Consider batching the produces.
- At minimum, add timing around the loop so the fan-out cost is visible.

Proposed fix:
~~~python
with metrics.timer("workflow_engine.detector.produce_results"):
    for result in detector_results.values():
        if result.result is not None:
            create_issue_occurrence_from_result(result)
~~~
